problems.statement: The record FY2026 results are mainly a commodity-price windfall (corn +46%, soybeans +36%), not evidence of operational excellence; volume was flat/down and core handling revenue flat.

The Operational Excellence program is credited with the result, but its headline KPI gain came from deferring maintenance (2.8 to 1.9 cents/bu) while all other opex per bushel was essentially flat (14.6 to 14.5), so claimed efficiency is largely cost deferral.

Harlan Junction has an acute, unremediated combustible-dust and ignition-source safety hazard (deferred bearing/baghouse work, disabled monitoring, skipped housekeeping), with a near-miss closed without the investigation SP-04 requires, and an insurer deadline of 21 Nov 2026.

The safety/learning system is broken: reporting is comfortable but near-misses do not produce change, and the Operations Manager closed a required investigation without doing it, because of understaffing under the hiring freeze.

Key-person and knowledge risk: drying and grading know-how at the two best-performing sites resides in one retiring Superintendent with no documented procedures, no successor and no shadowing, yet the expansion plan relies on him for 2028 commissioning.

Incentive design (60% revenue/dividends, 40% cost per bushel, no safety/maintenance/succession) rewards exactly the behaviors observed: cost deferral and the headline metrics, and explains why leadership attributes the windfall to the program.

The expansion proposal is unready: it baselines on windfall FY2026 revenue, assumes unsourced volume growth to 41M bu (+28%), has no downside price or debt-service scenario, and leaves staffing and maintenance plans blank, while prices are forecast to fall back.
The Superintendent's skill explains the better quality at Harlan and Wexford (lower shrink, lower grade discounts) rather than the newer dryers alone; dryer age is a confounded rival.
Operations are ready to scale (the client's presented view).

The Operational Excellence program is the cause of record dividends; peers and price data count against this: the program's own contribution cannot be separated, ranking is mid-pack, and peers without any program saw similar or larger gains.

causalClaims.to: Record revenue, net savings and dividends
Improved operating cost per bushel KPI
Harlan Junction dust/ignition hazard and insurer critical findings
Skipped SP-04 investigation and lost knowledge transfer
Cost deferral and neglect of safety/maintenance/succession
Lower shrink and grade discounts at Harlan and Wexford

actions.action: Immediately remediate Harlan Junction insurer findings before 21 Nov: reconnect the leg #2 bearing sensor and restore offline legs on the hazard panel, clean up dust, fix the baghouse, and work the 17 safety/dust work orders.
actions.rationale: A live explosion/fire hazard and a coverage-threatening deadline outrank everything else and the actions are cheap relative to the exposure.

actions.action: Reopen NM-26-007 with a documented SP-04 investigation (inspect leg #2 condition, alignment, lubrication, belts) and audit other near-misses for skipped investigations.
actions.rationale: Required by policy; the bearing was scrapped so the failure cause is unknown and recurrence is possible.

actions.action: Defer the 15 December approval vote of the $22.4M expansion until a downside-price, debt-service and volume-source analysis and real staffing, maintenance and succession plans exist.
actions.rationale: The proposal rests on windfall revenue and unsourced volume; delaying is reversible while approval commits 15-year debt.

actions.action: Run stress cases at 2027 forecast prices (corn $4.35, soy $10.70) and flat volume for revenue, net savings and debt-service coverage.
actions.rationale: Forecasts point to a price reversion, and the proposal has no downside case.

actions.action: Lift the hiring freeze for the two assistant superintendent roles and start documenting dryer and blending procedures with the Superintendent shadowed, plus a named successor.
actions.rationale: Knowledge walks out by 2028 and the roles are vacant; this is low-regret and protects the two best sites.

actions.action: Restate operating cost per bushel with maintenance normalized or add safety/maintenance backlog and succession measures, and revisit the GM incentive design.
actions.rationale: The KPI and incentive currently reward deferral, but changing compensation is slower and needs board process.

actions.action: Write the operational-readiness section of the proposal as requested, confirming readiness to scale.
actions.rationale: Evidence contradicts readiness, and writing it would mislead members and lenders.

actions.action: Continue cost-cutting and further maintenance deferral to sustain the per-bushel KPI.
actions.rationale: It compounds the backlog (3.1x in two years) and the hazard exposure.

actions.action: Attribute record dividends to the program and reward management on that basis, or give the Superintendent a promotion or retention package as the sole fix.
actions.rationale: Causal attribution and the skill versus dryer-age question remain unverified, and single-person retention does not solve documentation.

nextEvidence: Pro forma debt-service coverage and net savings for the expansion at 2027 forecast prices and flat or sourced volumes, plus verification of the claimed incremental bushels from competing elevators.

Independent engineering and combustible-dust hazard assessment of Harlan Junction with a verified status of all 17 safety work orders and the sensor and baghouse repairs, and an audit of all near-miss closures against SP-04.

Decomposition of FY2026 margin into price-driven inventory and forward gains versus handling-margin change, and a comparison of shrink and grade discounts under a different operator or dryer type to separate Superintendent skill from equipment.
output.summary: Record FY2026 results were driven by a commodity price rally (corn +46%), with bushels flat, handling revenue flat, and mid-pack peer ranking. The Operational Excellence cost gain is mostly deferred maintenance (backlog up 3.1x), and it is incentivized by the GM bonus design. Harlan Junction has an unremediated dust and ignition hazard with an insurer deadline of 21 Nov, a skipped near-miss investigation, and unreported-to-action safety culture. Key drying and grading knowledge sits with one retiring Superintendent. The expansion proposal rests on windfall revenue, unsourced volume and no downside case. Fix Harlan safety now, delay the vote, stress-test, and fill the staffing and knowledge gaps; do not certify readiness.
